findings.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:134 — Concurrent cache misses for the same key can build separate indexes because only cache assignment is locked. A slower build can overwrite an index containing newer events, causing stale search results. Add per-key build synchronization and recheck the cache before building.

pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go:216 — TotalDocs() iterates b.cache without locking after the event-processing goroutine starts, allowing concurrent map iteration and writes that can crash the process. Protect the iteration with cacheMu.RLock().

goldens.comment: A race condition in BuildIndex allows multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same expensive index for the same key. This is caused by moving the b.cacheMu lock from protecting the entire function to only protecting the final cache assignment.

Calling s.search.TotalDocs() here may race with concurrent index creation: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without synchronization, and the event watcher goroutine started just above could trigger BuildIndex writes concurrently, potentially causing a concurrent map read/write panic.

A slower build can overwrite an index containing newer events, causing stale search results. Add per-key build synchronization and recheck the cache before building.
per_golden_matches.reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the exact same race condition problem as the golden comment. Both describe: 1) Multiple goroutines can concurrently build the same index for the same key due to concurrent cache misses, 2) The root cause is that only the cache assignment is locked (not the entire build process), 3) This can lead to duplicate expensive index builds. The candidate adds additional detail about stale results from slower builds overwriting newer ones, but the core issue identified is the same race condition in BuildIndex.

per_golden_matches.matched_candidate: pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go:216 — TotalDocs() iterates b.cache without locking after the event-processing goroutine starts, allowing concurrent map iteration and writes that can crash the process. Protect the iteration with cacheMu.RLock().
per_golden_matches.reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the exact same problem as the golden comment: TotalDocs() iterates b.cache without synchronization, and this races with the event watcher goroutine that was started above which can trigger concurrent writes to the cache, potentially causing a crash/panic. Both comments point to the same race condition, same location (line 216 in the candidate matches the context of calling s.search.TotalDocs()), and same root cause (lack of locking during cache iteration while another goroutine may write to it).
